explanations: luna: The covenant here forbids shedding one another’s blood and expelling one another, مِيثَاقَكُمْ. Ayah 2:85 describes its violation and the later ransoming of captives; this row contributes the original binding that makes that reversal concrete.

luna: After 2:84’s covenant not to shed blood or expel one another, this ayah describes them doing both, then ransoming their captives, تُفَادُوهُمْ. It links a broken bond and kin-related bloodshed to release, while reversing the source section’s use of oath and freeing as a path toward care.

luna: Abraham asks, رَبِّ اجْعَلْ هَٰذَا بَلَدًا آمِنًا, that this town be secure and that its people receive fruit. It ties the source section’s oath over “this city” to the provision that the section’s passage turns toward the hungry.

luna: This account of righteousness gathers giving wealth to kin, orphans, and the poor, وَفِي الرِّقَابِ, keeping pledges, and patience in hardship. It closely gathers the source section’s release, feeding, and moral passage in one ayah. | terra: This description of righteousness places giving wealth to kin, orphans, the poor, and travelers beside وَفِى ٱلرِّقَابِ, uniting the two works the section reads as the content of kaffāra.

luna: This retaliation ruling lets the victim’s brother forgive and calls for compensation to be paid fairly, فَمَنْ عُفِيَ لَهُ مِنْ أَخِيهِ شَيْءٌ. It supplies a concrete Quranic scene of a slain person’s kin receiving a release from retaliation, adjacent to the section’s qasāma definition. | terra: The homicide ruling gives the slain person's brother authority to pardon and receive fair payment, supplying a Quranic legal setting of killing, kin, released claim, and compensation close to the qasāma background.

luna: This verse places feeding a poor person, فِدْيَةٌ طَعَامُ مِسْكِينٍ, as a compensation alongside a fasting obligation. Its arrangement differs from the source section’s oath expiation, where fasting is the fallback, but it gives a specific parallel between fasting and feeding. | terra: For those unable to fast, the fidya is feeding a poor person; fasting and feeding appear as substitutable responses to incapacity, as they do in the section's expiation passages.

terra: The pilgrimage fidya offers fasting, charity, or sacrifice as compensatory alternatives, paralleling the measured menu of acts used to release an oath, though this breach is ritual rather than verbal.

luna: The source section’s root y-m-n appears in عُرْضَةً لِّأَيْمَانِكُمْ; this verse says not to make Allah an obstacle to righteousness, reverence, or peacemaking. It marks the boundary the image needs: an oath should not block the good that the section presents as feeding and mercy. | terra: The command not to make God's name in one's oaths an obstacle to goodness, piety, and reconciliation sets a boundary: an oath-knot must not be used to bar the good deeds that give it moral content.

luna: This ayah distinguishes idle oaths, اللَّغْوِ فِي أَيْمَانِكُمْ, from what hearts deliberately bind. That boundary clarifies why the section’s image of a tied oath and its expiation concerns an intended bond, not every passing utterance. | terra: God does not hold people to account for unintentional speech in oaths but does for what hearts earn; beside 2:224, it distinguishes an unbound utterance from a morally effective oath.

luna: This names a concrete oath not to approach one’s wife, يُؤْلُونَ مِن نِّسَائِهِمْ, gives a four-month term, and says return is open. It makes the oath’s resolution and the alternative of remaining bound a lived legal scene. | terra: The waiting period for those who swear abstinence from their wives stages an oath that creates a temporary bond and allows a return, a legal case of pledged speech requiring resolution.

luna: After 2:226’s oath concerning marital relations, this verse gives the other path: if the couple decides on divorce, Allah hears and knows. It completes the boundary between returning from the oath and proceeding to separation. | terra: If those who swore abstinence resolve on divorce, this ayah states the alternative outcome to return in 2:226, completing that legal oath's required resolution.

luna: The verse names the knot of marriage, عُقْدَةَ النِّكَاحِ, and sets a limit on resolving it until the prescribed term. It is not an oath, but it gives a concrete legal knot beside the source section’s image of an oath-bound knot and its loosening.

terra: The divorce ruling speaks of ٱلَّذِى بِيَدِهِ عُقْدَةُ ٱلنِّكَاحِ: a legal knot held in a hand and capable of being relinquished, concretely joining the section's hand, knot, and release imagery.
terra: Whatever people spend and whatever vow they make are named together under God's knowledge; the next ayah then joins alms to expiation, making vowed speech and giving adjacent.

luna: The source section’s root k-f-r appears in يُكَفِّرُ عَنكُم مِّن سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ: this verse joins giving charity to the poor with Allah’s covering of some misdeeds. It directly meets the section’s claim that provision for the needy can cover the evil of a spoken wrong. | terra: Secret alms delivered to the poor are said to be better and to يُكَفِّرُ عَنكُم مِّن سَيِّـَٔاتِكُمْ; this directly joins provision for the poor to the section's root-sense of covering a fault.

terra: The wife of Imran vows what is in her womb as مُحَرَّرًا; the form shares the liberation root with taḥrīr al-raqaba and binds a vow to dedication, although it denotes consecrated service rather than manumission.

luna: The source section’s root y-m-n appears with Allah’s covenant, عَهْدَ اللَّهِ وَأَيْمَانَهُمْ, which this verse says people sell for a small price, losing a share of the Hereafter. It reverses the oath’s role as a path toward the successful group. | terra: Those who trade God's covenant and their oaths for a small price make the oath yield profit; the section's kaffāra reverses that economy by requiring one to spend, feed, fast, or free after breach.

luna: At the time of an inheritance division, الْقِسْمَةَ, relatives, orphans, and the poor are present and are to be given something. This concretizes the source section’s dictionary account of qasāma as oaths distributed among a dead person’s kin, while joining division to its needy recipients. | terra: At the division, ٱلْقِسْمَةَ, of an estate, relatives, orphans, and needy people present are to receive provision; literal division thus meets the vulnerable recipients of the surah's passage.

luna: This warns that those who consume orphan property unjustly are consuming fire and will burn in a blaze. It sharply reverses the section’s feeding and care for the orphan, and joins that reversal to its final fire image.

terra: وَٱلَّذِينَ عَقَدَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ joins a binding act to right hands and then commands giving the parties their allotted share, bringing together the section's knot, yamin, and division senses.

luna: For accidental killing, this verse joins تَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُؤْمِنَةٍ with compensation to the victim’s family and fasting if freedom is unavailable. It is not the qasāma procedure, but it concretely meets the source’s slain-kin definition and 90:13’s freeing-neck image. | terra: For accidental killing, this ayah requires freeing a believing neck and, when that is impossible, two consecutive months of fasting; the same two acts repair a grave breach rather than a broken oath.
terra: The command أَوْفُوا۟ بِٱلْعُقُودِ establishes the obligation of fulfilling binding knots at the opening of the same surah that later regulates knotted oaths and their release.

luna: The source section’s root ح ل ل appears as حَلَلْتُمْ for coming out of pilgrimage consecration, after which hunting is permitted. It is a different legal release from an oath, but concretely shows the root’s movement from restriction to release.

luna: After taking a covenant, Allah promises, لَأُكَفِّرَنَّ عَنكُمْ سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ, to cover the people’s sins if they fulfill its terms. This links a binding commitment to the source section’s expiatory sense of root ك ف ر. | terra: God's covenant with Israel joins alms and a goodly loan to the promise لَأُكَفِّرَنَّ عَنكُمْ سَيِّـَٔاتِكُمْ; binding commitment, provision, and the covering of wrongs occur in one ayah.

luna: The ayah says that whoever waives a claim in retaliation receives expiation, فَهُوَ كَفَّارَةٌ لَّهُ. This joins the source section’s root k-f-r with a concrete homicide-and-pardon ruling, complementing its qasāma definition about oaths among a slain person’s kin. | terra: فَمَن تَصَدَّقَ بِهِ فَهُوَ كَفَّارَةٌ لَّهُ makes the charitable surrender of a retaliation claim a kaffāra, so releasing a right itself becomes a covering for wrong.

terra: أَقْسَمُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ places qasam and aymān together for one emphatic oath, while the collapse of the swearers' deeds exposes the gap between their bound words and action.
terra: The command not to forbid the good things God has made lawful supplies the ح ل ل boundary immediately before the oath-and-kaffāra ruling in 5:89.
terra: The command to eat the lawful and good provision God has given completes 5:87's lawful/forbidden scene before 5:89 explains what to do with binding oaths.

luna: The source section points to this ruling itself: it names bound oaths, عَقَّدتُّمُ الْأَيْمَانَ, and their kaffāra is feeding ten poor, freeing a neck, or fasting three days when unable. It supplies the legal passage from oath to feeding and release. | terra: This ayah states the section's whole mechanism: deliberately knotted oaths, their kaffāra, feeding ten poor people, freeing a neck, and three days of fasting when those means are unavailable.

luna: For killing game during pilgrimage, this verse names كَفَّارَةٌ طَعَامُ مَسَاكِينَ or fasting. The offense differs from a broken oath, but it gives another concrete Quranic legal passage where expiation is carried by food and fasting. | terra: The hunting violation is repaired by an equivalent offering, كَفَّارَةٌ طَعَامُ مَسَاكِينَ, or equivalent fasting, closely matching the substitution structure of oath-expiation.

luna: This legal procedure uses sworn testimony, فَيُقْسِمَانِ بِاللَّهِ, when death intervenes and explicitly mentions a near relative. It is not qasāma, but its death-and-kin setting gives a concrete Quranic counterpart to the source section’s dictionary account of oaths among a slain person’s kin. | terra: In a deathbed-estate dispute, two detained witnesses فَيُقْسِمَانِ بِٱللَّهِ; this judicially assigned oath closely realizes the section's qasāma background of shared oaths around death and claims.
terra: If the first witnesses are found culpable, two others take their place and swear; the replacement and redistribution of the oath sharpen the qasāma sense developed in the section.
terra: أَوْ يَخَافُوٓا۟ أَن تُرَدَّ أَيْمَانٌۢ بَعْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ explicitly describes oaths returned after prior oaths, completing the judicial oath sequence of 5:106-107.

terra: They swear their strongest oaths that they will believe if a sign comes, yet the reply warns that the sign will not produce belief; oath and response to divine signs meet as the reverse of 90:19's settled disbelief.
terra: This ayah commands giving the harvest's due on the day it is gathered; it supplies the positive harvest practice that the oath-bound garden owners in 68:17-24 deliberately reverse.

luna: This verse protects the orphan’s property, مَالَ الْيَتِيمِ, commands just speech even when a relative is concerned, and ends by commanding fulfillment of Allah’s covenant. It gathers the orphan, kin, and binding obligation that the section brings together through qasāma and feeding.
terra: The deceiver swears to the first pair that he is a sincere adviser, making qasam the vehicle of a harmful lie rather than a binding word repaired by truthful action.
terra: People once judged by an oath to be beyond God's mercy are commanded to enter the Garden; the outcome explicitly overturns the swearers' verdict.

luna: A designated share of the gains is assigned to relatives, orphans, the needy, and travelers, وَلِذِي الْقُرْبَىٰ وَالْيَتَامَىٰ وَالْمَسَاكِينِ. This gives another concrete allocation of resources to the kin and poor who appear in the source section’s qasāma definition and feeding passage.
terra: نَّكَثُوٓا۟ أَيْمَانَهُم names enemies who break their oaths after covenant; it is the culpable breach for which the section's lawful release and covering provide a sharp boundary.
terra: This continuation again names a people who broke their oaths and couples the breach with an attempted expulsion of the Messenger, showing the hostile act carried by the broken word.

luna: The prescribed shares of charity include the poor, needy, and those in bondage, فِي الرِّقَابِ. This connects the section’s allocation sense of qasāma with its specific movement from the oath to feeding and freeing. | terra: The prescribed alms categories include the poor and needy together with وَفِى ٱلرِّقَابِ, again placing feeding-support and release of bound people within one distribution.

luna: The verse says they swear they did not speak, though they did speak a word of disbelief, كَلِمَةَ الْكُفْرِ. It joins a false oath to the source section’s root ك ف ر, showing the contrary case of a word and oath that are not repaired. | terra: They swear that they did not speak, although the ayah says they uttered كَلِمَةَ ٱلْكُفْرِ; oath, a harmful utterance, and kufr converge here without the reparative deed developed in the section.
terra: A group pledges that, if God gives them bounty, they will give charity and become righteous; the ayah directly binds a pledged word to provision for others.
terra: When bounty arrives they become stingy and turn away, so the promised charity is withheld rather than performed as the deed demanded by the word.
terra: Their resulting hypocrisy is traced to breaking what they promised God and lying, making the moral consequence arise from the gap between pledged speech and action.
terra: إِنَّ ٱلْحَسَنَاتِ يُذْهِبْنَ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ states the general relation enacted concretely by the section's kaffāra: a required good deed removes the trace of a wrong.
terra: At judgment people are reminded that they had sworn they would never pass away; reality dissolves their confident oath and exposes its false object.
terra: ٱلْمُقْتَسِمِينَ names the partitioners; on the division reading made explicit by 15:91, it preserves the ق س م sense of splitting rather than swearing.
terra: ٱلَّذِينَ جَعَلُوا۟ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ عِضِينَ explains the partitioners as people who made the Quran into portions, a destructive use of division that contrasts with reparative apportionment.
terra: They swear their strongest oaths that God will not raise the dead; the human oath asserts denial, while the divine oath formula of the section bears witness rather than conceals unbelief.

luna: The source section’s root y-m-n appears in الْأَيْمَانَ بَعْدَ تَوْكِيدِهَا; this verse commands keeping Allah’s covenant and not breaking oaths after confirmation. It gives the binding side of the section’s knot image. | terra: The command not to break oaths after confirming them supplies the boundary to lawful taḥilla: release is divinely regulated, while arbitrary undoing after making God guarantor is condemned.

luna: The warning against becoming like the woman who unravels her yarn after firm spinning, نَقَضَتْ غَزْلَهَا, is an explicit image of undoing what was made secure; 16:91 supplies the oath context, while this verse supplies the unraveling simile. | terra: The woman who unravels her firmly spun yarn is the concrete simile for taking oaths as deceit; it gives the section's oath-knot an explicit wrongful unravelling.

luna: The verse warns against making أَيْمَانَكُمْ دَخَلًا between people, because feet may slip after having been firm. That reverses the section’s oath as a binding that can be released through a divinely prescribed remedy. | terra: The repeated ban on making oaths a means of deception adds the consequence of a foot slipping after firmness, contrasting a treacherous loosening with prescribed release.

luna: The command not to trade Allah’s covenant, عَهْدَ اللَّهِ, for a small price gives a material-gain reversal: the garden owners’ oath is aimed at keeping the harvest for themselves, while this verse names covenant as worth more than immediate gain. | terra: Following the bans on deceptive oaths, this ayah forbids selling God's covenant for a small price; it contrasts profit from a pledged word with the material cost of repairing one.

terra: The command not to make one's hand chained to one's neck, nor extend it without limit, sets hand, neck, bondage, and giving in one measured scene; it is a bodily counterimage to freeing a neck through expenditure.

luna: The verse gives the guardian of a person killed unjustly authority, لِوَلِيِّهِ سُلْطَانًا, while forbidding excess in retaliation. This grounds the source section’s qasāma reference to the slain person’s close kin in a Quranic rule about their standing.

luna: The verse joins care of the orphan’s property, مَالَ الْيَتِيمِ, to the command to fulfill the covenant, وَأَوْفُوا بِالْعَهْدِ. This is a specific pairing of the section’s vulnerable kin and binding-promise themes.

luna: The verse says people will be given their records in the right hand, بِيَمِينِهِ, at the gathering. This is another concrete right-hand sign of outcome that grounds the source section’s yamin/hand association.
terra: Mary says she has vowed a fast to the Merciful and therefore will not speak that day; vow, fasting, and restrained utterance meet here, although the fast fulfills rather than expiates the vow.
terra: Moses' staff is literally held بِيَمِينِكَ; this supplies the concrete right-hand sense from which the section's dictionary says yamin as 'oath' is borrowed.

luna: The source section’s knot-and-untying account is made literal in Moses’s prayer to loosen a knot from his tongue, وَاحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِّن لِّسَانِي. Here release enables speech to be understood, a precise nonlexical parallel to loosening an oath-knot. | terra: Moses asks وَٱحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِّن لِّسَانِى; the Quranic act of untying a knot from the organ of speech gives concrete form to the section's 'untying the knot of an oath.'

luna: After Moses asks in 20:27 for the knot of his tongue to be loosened, this ayah states the purpose: that they understand his speech, يَفْقَهُوا قَوْلِي. It completes a precise image of release applied to speech, beside the source section’s oath-knot and its untying. | terra: لِسَانِى in 20:27 is followed by يَفْقَهُوا۟ قَوْلِى, confirming that the untied knot serves intelligible speech and thus sharpening the section's knot-of-an-utterance analogy.

terra: Pilgrims are told to eat from sacrificial animals and feed the destitute poor; immediately before fulfillment of vows in 22:29, provision for the hungry becomes part of carrying a consecrated commitment through.
terra: وَلْيُوفُوا۟ نُذُورَهُمْ commands pilgrims to fulfill their vows immediately after 22:28's feeding of the destitute, creating a specific vow-and-provision sequence.
terra: A husband with no witnesses must give four testimonies by God that he speaks truth, beginning a judicially apportioned oath procedure that recalls the section's qasāma definition.
terra: The accuser's fifth testimony invokes God's curse if he lies, showing the added consequence that seals the repeated sworn speech of 24:6.
terra: The accused wife averts punishment by answering with four testimonies by God that he lies; the oath burden is now redistributed to the opposing party.
terra: Her fifth testimony invokes God's wrath if the husband is truthful, completing the reciprocal judicial oath sequence.

luna: Here people are told not to swear off giving, وَلَا يَأْتَلِ, to relatives, the poor, and emigrants, and are urged to pardon. This reverses the garden owners’ oath to keep the poor out and aligns oath-release with renewed generosity. | terra: Those with means are forbidden to let an oath stop them giving to relatives, needy people, and emigrants, and are told to pardon; this directly stages an oath-knot released so provision and forgiveness can resume.

luna: The verse encourages a contractual route out of bondage, فَكَاتِبُوهُمْ, and calls for material help from what Allah has provided. This is a concrete emancipation scene that complements the source section’s freeing-neck branch, though it is not an oath expiation. | terra: Those whom right hands possess and who seek a freedom contract are to be contracted and given God's wealth; the ayah brings literal أَيْمَان, liberation, and financial provision into one scene.
terra: After people swear their strongest oaths that they will go out if commanded, the reply قُل لَّا تُقْسِمُوا۟ طَاعَةٌ مَّعْرُوفَةٌ places recognizable obedience above emphatic speech alone.
terra: The she-camel has one water-share and the people another on an appointed day; without using qasam itself, the scene concretely enacts the apportioned share behind the section's division sense.

terra: تَقَاسَمُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ begins a mutual oath to attack a man and his household by night and then deny it to his guardian, darkly realizing the qasāma association of shared oaths, killing, and the slain person's kin.
terra: The guilty swear at the Hour that they remained only an hour, so an oath again carries a false claim precisely when moral accounting makes its falsity plain.
terra: They swear that a warner would make them better guided than any other community, but when one comes it only increases aversion; the action contradicts the pledged claim.

terra: Those who disbelieve answer a command to spend by asking whether they should feed someone God could feed; كَفَرُوا۟ and refusal to feed meet on the opposite side of the section's kaffāra-by-feeding image.

luna: The verse gives Job a way to act without breaking his oath: take a bundle in the hand and strike with it, “and do not break your oath,” وَلَا تَحْنَثْ. It is a divine solution to a sworn obligation, complementing the section’s account of prescribed oath-release.

luna: The verse uses the source section’s root ك ف ر, لِيُكَفِّرَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ, for covering the worst of what people did and rewarding their best. This is the same covering sense that the section draws from kaffāra, though here the covered deeds are general rather than a broken oath.

luna: The source section’s root ق س م also occurs in the statement that Allah apportioned livelihoods among people, قَسَمْنَا. In its ordinary allocation sense, the verse adds a provision-and-distribution parallel to the image’s feeding of the poor. | terra: نَحْنُ قَسَمْنَا بَيْنَهُم مَّعِيشَتَهُمْ uses ق س م for God's division of livelihood, making concrete the section's claim that the oath-root first carries apportionment.

luna: After captives are firmly bound in battle, the verse allows release, فِدَاءً, or pardon. This is not oath-expiation, but its concrete movement from bondage to release echoes the freeing-neck branch of the image. | terra: After captives are firmly bound, the command permits gracious release or ransom; the ayah makes loosening a human bond concrete and sets release against its opening image of struck necks.

luna: This verse pairs Allah’s covering believers’ sins, وَيُكَفِّرَ عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ, with their admission to gardens, using the same expiatory root ك ف ر as the source section. Ayah 48:6 supplies the opposite group, so this row contributes the saved side of that contrast.

luna: This verse describes the opposing group and the Fire, جَهَنَّمَ, prepared for them. It contributes the negative side of the believers’ covering and garden outcome in 48:5, paralleling the section’s right/left and fire ending.

terra: The pledge is enacted by hands, يَدُ ٱللَّهِ فَوْقَ أَيْدِيهِمْ, and the ayah names the one who breaks it with نَّكَثَ; it stages both the bodily source of yamin and the breaking of a binding pledge.

terra: فَٱلْمُقَسِّمَاتِ أَمْرًا is itself the final object in a divine oath sequence: the oath is grammatically made by those who distribute, an unusually exact Quranic meeting of qasam and division.
terra: تِلْكَ إِذًا قِسْمَةٌ ضِيزَىٰ condemns an inequitable division, supplying the unjust boundary of the section's claim that qasam grows from apportionment.
terra: أَنَّ ٱلْمَآءَ قِسْمَةٌۢ بَيْنَهُمْ uses the oath-root's division sense for an allotted water-share, another concrete instance of the apportionment from which the section derives qasam.

luna: This uses the same label as 90:18, أَصْحَابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ, for the people of the right. The exact group-name grounds the source section’s link from al-maymana to the right side. | terra: وَأَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَيْمَنَةِ names the same fortunate company as 90:18 and places it within the final threefold division of humanity.
luna: This names the opposing group as أَصْحَابُ الْمَشْأَمَةِ. It supplies the left-side boundary paired with 56:8 and with the section’s companions of the right versus the left.

luna: The verse again names أَصْحَابُ الْيَمِينِ and opens their description. It gives a repeated right-side designation using the source section’s root y-m-n and ties it to a favorable group. | terra: وَأَصْحَابُ ٱلْيَمِينِ asks after the people of the right and begins to display their provision, unfolding the right-side sense behind the section's meymene/yamin link.

luna: Within the right-hand group’s description opened in 56:27, this verse assigns the preceding garden scene to أَصْحَابُ الْيَمِينِ. Its contribution is to identify that reward as belonging to the right-hand group.

luna: This ayah names the companions of the left, أَصْحَابُ الشِّمَالِ, the opposing group whose counterpart appears in the source section’s closing division between the fortunate side and the condemned side.

luna: The left group’s scene continues with scorching wind and boiling water, فِي سَمُومٍ وَحَمِيمٍ. Its own contribution is the concrete punishment completing the group label in 56:41 and echoing the sealed Fire at the end of the source surah.

luna: The next ayah adds a shade of black smoke, وَظِلٍّ مِّن يَحْمُومٍ, to the left group’s punishment begun in 56:41. This further detail extends the contrast with the source section’s right-hand group.

luna: This says that the smoke-shade is neither cool nor beneficial, لَا بَارِدٍ وَلَا كَرِيمٍ. It completes the deprivation in 56:41–43, a specific opposite to the section’s passage through feeding and mercy.

luna: The divine formula فَلَا أُقْسِمُ introduces an oath by the stars’ settings, repeating the distinctive opening formula the section notes at 90:1. | terra: فَلَآ أُقْسِمُ بِمَوَاقِعِ ٱلنُّجُومِ is the same divine formula as 90:1, now swearing by the positions of the stars.

luna: This next ayah calls the oath in 56:75 عظِيمٌ, a great oath. Its contribution is to interpret the oath’s stature, completing the link begun there. | terra: This ayah calls the preceding utterance لَقَسَمٌ ... عَظِيمٌ, supplying God's own assessment that such a qasam is immense.
luna: At death, the verse again classifies a person as among أَصْحَابِ الْيَمِينِ. This applies the source section’s right-side label to the final encounter.
luna: The next ayah greets the person, فَسَلَامٌ لَّكَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ الْيَمِينِ, with peace from the companions of the right. Its contribution is the welcome attached to the group named in 56:90.
luna: The believers’ light runs before them and at their right hands, وَبِأَيْمَانِهِمْ. This gives the source section’s right-hand association a visible image of guidance and safety.

luna: The verse identifies the zihar saying as مُنكَرًا مِّنَ الْقَوْلِ and false; 58:3 names its expiation. Its contribution is to identify the spoken wrong that the section’s freeing and feeding imagery can cover. | terra: This ayah calls ẓihār an objectionable false utterance; it identifies the spoken wrong that the neck-release and feeding in 58:3-4 are then required to answer.

luna: The section cites this expiation: after the zihar utterance, the man must perform تَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ before the spouses touch again. It gives a second concrete setting for release as repair after speech. | terra: After a speaker retracts ẓihār, this ayah requires تَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ before the spouses touch; it directly stages a harmful utterance answered by freeing a neck.

luna: This is the continuation of 58:3: if the man cannot free someone, he performs فَإِطْعَامُ سِتِّينَ مِسْكِينًا. Its own contribution is the food branch, joining expiation to the section’s feeding passage. | terra: This continuation replaces the unavailable neck-release with two months of fasting, then with feeding sixty poor people, reproducing the section's ladder of compensatory acts.

luna: The source section’s root y-m-n appears in the hypocrites’ shield-oaths, أَيْمَانَهُمْ جُنَّةً, which they use to block Allah’s path. This is a cover that conceals wrongdoing, reversing the section’s expiation that covers a broken oath’s harm. | terra: The same phrase, ٱتَّخَذُوٓا۟ أَيْمَانَهُمْ جُنَّةً, appears in the surah whose opening prescribes neck-release and feeding, sharply opposing false oath-as-cover to reparative action.

luna: This verse distributes public wealth to relatives, orphans, the poor, and travelers, كَيْ لَا يَكُونَ دُولَةً بَيْنَ الْأَغْنِيَاءِ مِنكُمْ, so it will not circulate only among the rich. It gives a specific economic reversal to the garden owners’ oath excluding the poor from a share.

luna: This repeats the shield-oath image, أَيْمَانَهُمْ جُنَّةً, from the source section’s y-m-n root, now used to obstruct Allah’s way. It is the reversal in the hypocrites’ own passage: oath as concealment rather than repair. | terra: ٱتَّخَذُوٓا۟ أَيْمَانَهُمْ جُنَّةً turns oaths into a shield for obstructing God's path; this is a corrupt 'cover' made from the oath itself, unlike kaffāra's deed that covers a breach.

luna: The next ayah says they believed and then disbelieved, كَفَرُوا, and their hearts were sealed. Beside 63:2’s oath-shield, it puts the source section’s root ك ف ر in its denial sense against its expiation-and-covering sense.

luna: At the Day of Gathering, Allah covers believers’ sins, يُكَفِّرْ عَنْهُ سَيِّئَاتِهِ, and admits them to gardens. This is the positive outcome on the same root ك ف ر as the section’s kaffāra; 64:10 supplies the contrasting fate.

luna: This says those who disbelieve, كَفَرُوا, and deny Allah’s signs remain in the Fire. Its own contribution is the condemned group and sealed outcome, matching the section’s contrast at 90:19–20; 64:9 gives the covered-sin counterpart.

luna: This immediately precedes 66:2: the Prophet is asked لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ مَا أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكَ, and the next ayah prescribes release of oaths. This verse gives the particular self-imposed restriction to which that release responds. | terra: The Prophet is asked why he forbids what God made lawful, مَا أَحَلَّ ٱللَّهُ لَكَ; the next ayah's oath-release thus restores what an utterance had restricted.

luna: The source section’s dictionary form tahillat is explicit here: Allah prescribes the dissolution of your oaths, تَحِلَّةَ أَيْمَانِكُمْ. This directly grounds the knot-and-release image in a divine ruling. | terra: قَدْ فَرَضَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ تَحِلَّةَ أَيْمَانِكُمْ names the divinely provided release of oaths with the same taḥilla from ح ل ل that the section uses for untying the oath-knot.

luna: The verse uses the source section’s root ك ف ر, يُكَفِّرَ, for covering believers’ sins and says their light runs before them and at their right hands. It brings the section’s expiation and right-hand associations into one final-judgment scene. | terra: Sincere repentance is promised the covering of wrongs, while the forgiven believers' light runs at their right hands; in the same surah as oath-release, this ayah joins takfīr to the favorable yamin image.

luna: The garden owners swear, إِذْ أَقْسَمُوا, to harvest in the morning. The source section explicitly contrasts this human oath, whose aim is to keep the poor from the garden, with the oath that opens a way through feeding. | terra: The garden owners أَقْسَمُوا۟ لَيَصْرِمُنَّهَا swear to harvest at dawn; their human oath opens a plan whose purpose is the reverse of the poor-feeding passage introduced by the divine oath in surah 90.

luna: They make no exception, وَلَا يَسْتَثْنُونَ, to their plan. This contributes the unqualified, closed character of the oath whose aim is disclosed in 68:24. | terra: وَلَا يَسْتَثْنُونَ says the garden owners made no exception; it shows the oath-plan closed against qualification before its exclusion of the poor is voiced.

luna: After their exclusionary oath, a blast from their Lord, طَائِفٌ مِّن رَّبِّكَ, visits the garden while they sleep. It begins the reversal of the harvest they intended to reserve; the section’s linked scene is 68:17 and its aim is stated in 68:24. | terra: A visitation from the Lord circles the garden while its owners sleep, interrupting the oath-bound plan before they can exclude the poor.

luna: The garden is found ruined, كَالصَّرِيمِ, so the planned private harvest disappears. This is the outcome reversing the oath in 68:17 and withholding plan in 68:24. | terra: By morning the garden has become stripped and dark, so the intended harvest that motivated the oath is itself removed.

luna: At dawn they call one another, فَتَنَادَوْا مُصْبِحِينَ, to carry out the harvest plan sworn in 68:17. This row contributes the move from oath to morning action in the garden owners’ reversal of the section’s food passage.

luna: They tell each other to go early to their crop, اغْدُوا عَلَىٰ حَرْثِكُمْ, if they mean to harvest it. This supplies the concrete action the oath in 68:17 anticipated, in the plan that excludes the poor.
luna: The owners set out وَهُمْ يَتَخَافَتُونَ, speaking privately. This contributes the concealed execution of the exclusionary plan stated in 68:24, reversing the section’s feeding passage.

luna: The plan is stated: no poor person is to enter the garden that day, أَن لَّا يَدْخُلَنَّهَا ... مِسْكِينٌ. This is the exact reversal of the section’s oath-to-food passage. | terra: أَن لَّا يَدْخُلَنَّهَا ٱلْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكُم مِّسْكِينٌ states the oath's object: keeping every poor person out, the exact reversal of making food for the needy the difficult pass.

luna: They go out غَدَوْا عَلَىٰ حَرْدٍ, resolved and thinking they have power over the harvest. This completes the execution of the plan sworn in 68:17 to reserve the garden for themselves. | terra: They go out at dawn intent and confident of their power, showing the oath moving from binding speech into the attempted act described in 68:24.

luna: After the plan sworn in 68:17 and exclusion stated in 68:24, they see the ruined garden and say إِنَّا لَضَالُّونَ, thinking they have lost their way. This is their first recognition that the promised harvest has vanished.

luna: They correct themselves: rather, بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ, they have been deprived. Its own contribution is to name the loss that reverses the plan in 68:17 and the exclusion in 68:24. | terra: The owners conclude that they themselves are deprived; the deprivation they planned for the poor returns upon them.

luna: After the exclusion plan in 68:24 fails, they say سُبْحَانَ رَبِّنَا and admit wrongdoing. This may echo the image’s movement from a wrongful utterance toward return, though the verse does not prescribe the oath-expatiation law discussed in the section. | terra: They glorify their Lord and confess that they were wrongdoers, supplying the penitential verbal response after the wrongful oath and its collapse.

terra: They hope their Lord will replace the garden with something better and turn their desire toward Him; this closes the oath story with repentance and hoped-for replacement, though no material kaffāra is stated.

luna: After the oath of 68:17 and the exclusion stated in 68:24, this verse identifies the garden’s loss as punishment and warns that عَذَابَ الْآخِرَةِ is greater. It completes the reversal of the owners’ plan to hoard the harvest.
terra: أَمْ لَكُمْ أَيْمَانٌ عَلَيْنَا بَالِغَةٌ asks whether the claimants possess binding oaths from God lasting to resurrection, explicitly presenting an oath as an enduring guarantee.

luna: Here the record is given in the right hand, بِيَمِينِهِ. It makes the source section’s hand-sense of yamin concrete in a judgment scene. | terra: Receiving one's record بِيَمِينِهِ realizes the fortunate right-hand sense behind أصحاب الميمنة; later in the same surah come both failure to feed the poor and the formula فَلَآ أُقْسِمُ.

luna: The opposite person receives the record in the left hand, بِشِمَالِهِ. Its own contribution is the reversal of the right-hand reception in 69:19, matching the section’s contrast between the right and left groups.

luna: This ayah says the condemned person did not believe in Allah, لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ; 69:34 then specifies that he did not urge food for the poor. This row contributes disbelief as the stance behind that specific withholding. | terra: The condemned person's failure to believe in God is paired in the next ayah with failure to urge food for the poor, reversing the section's joining of faith and merciful action.

luna: The condemned person does not urge feeding the poor, طَعَامِ الْمِسْكِينِ. This is a direct opposite of the food that the source section makes the passage through expiation. | terra: وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ ٱلْمِسْكِينِ names the omitted act that helps explain his judgment, directly opposing the section's feeding scene.
terra: فَلَآ أُقْسِمُ بِمَا تُبْصِرُونَ reproduces the formula and begins a paired oath by what the hearers see and do not see.
terra: وَمَا لَا تُبْصِرُونَ completes 69:38's paired oath-object, extending the same divine formula from the visible to the unseen.

luna: This states the condition of fabricating words against Allah, تَقَوَّلَ عَلَيْنَا بَعْضَ الْأَقَاوِيلِ, before the right-hand seizure in 69:45. It contrasts the source section’s true divine oath with false speech attributed to God. | terra: The hypothetical uttering of fabricated sayings against God supplies a grave false-speech scene shortly after the divine oath formula in 69:38.

luna: In the conditional warning begun in 69:44 about inventing words against Allah, this ayah says the Messenger would be seized بِالْيَمِينِ. The source section’s root y-m-n is here the literal right hand, a distinct but pointed counterpart because its discussion joins oath and hand. | terra: The next ayah says the false speaker would be seized باليمين, plausibly by the right hand or by power; either reading gives a boundary case for the section's yamin-as-hand claim, but the lexical sense is interpretively disputed.

luna: The warning continues with cutting the aorta, الْوَتِينَ, after the seizure in 69:45. This is the consequence completing that false-speech scene, a severe reversal of the section’s remedial feeding and freeing after a broken oath.
terra: فَلَآ أُقْسِمُ بِرَبِّ ٱلْمَشَارِقِ وَٱلْمَغَارِبِ is another direct occurrence of the section's divine oath formula.
terra: كُلُّ نَفْسٍۭ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ رَهِينَةٌ pictures every soul held in pledge by its deeds; the following exception for the people of the right links binding and moral consequence.

luna: The verse identifies a saved group as أَصْحَابُ الْيَمِينِ, a repeated right-side designation that clarifies the favorable sense of the source section’s al-maymana. | terra: إِلَّآ أَصْحَابَ ٱلْيَمِينِ releases the people of the right from the pledged condition in 74:38, joining the section's right-side title to release from a bond.
terra: The people questioned from punishment confess وَلَمْ نَكُ نُطْعِمُ ٱلْمِسْكِينَ; in the same passage that exempts أصحاب اليمين from pledge, failure to feed marks the other outcome.

luna: This repeats the section’s opening formula لَا أُقْسِمُ, here swearing by Resurrection Day. The shared form makes this a direct parallel in the act of divine oath-making. | terra: لَآ أُقْسِمُ بِيَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ repeats the section's exact divine opening formula, changing only the object of the oath.

luna: This continues the same formula with an oath by the self-reproaching soul. Its own contribution is a second object of the repeated oath, completing the sequence opened in 75:1. | terra: وَلَآ أُقْسِمُ بِٱلنَّفْسِ ٱللَّوَّامَةِ immediately repeats the same formula for a second oath-object, confirming that 75:1 is a sustained oath opening.
terra: يُوفُونَ بِٱلنَّذْرِ presents fidelity to a vowed word, and the next ayah shows that fidelity embodied in feeding the vulnerable.

luna: The righteous give food, وَيُطْعِمُونَ الطَّعَامَ, to the needy, orphan, and captive. This is a direct social scene parallel to the source section’s feeding of the poor and freeing of the neck. | terra: Feeding a poor person, an orphan, and a captive in one act gathers the section's food, orphan, needy person, and bound-neck scenes around the vow of 76:7.

luna: Following 76:8’s feeding of the needy, this ayah gives the feeders’ stated motive: they feed for Allah’s sake, لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ, seeking neither payment nor thanks. That motive contrasts with the garden owners’ self-serving oath and completes the feeding scene with its own contribution.
terra: فَلَآ أُقْسِمُ بِٱلْخُنَّسِ directly repeats the formula with the retreating heavenly bodies as its object.
terra: ٱلْجَوَارِ ٱلْكُنَّسِ continues and identifies the heavenly bodies invoked by the oath formula in 81:15.

luna: This again gives the record to a person in the right hand, بِيَمِينِهِ, and promises an easy reckoning. It connects the section’s right-hand sense of yamin to favorable judgment. | terra: The one given his record بِيَمِينِهِ embodies the favorable right-hand image, and the same surah later uses the section's exact oath formula at 84:16.
luna: This contrasts the right-hand recipient in 84:7 with one given the record وَرَاءَ ظَهْرِهِ. The ayah provides the opposite side of the right-hand judgment image.

luna: This says the person whose record came from behind will enter سَعِيرًا. Its own contribution is the punishment for the negative judgment outcome, echoing the sealed Fire in the section’s final ayah.
terra: فَلَآ أُقْسِمُ بِٱلشَّفَقِ directly repeats the formula with twilight as its first oath-object.
terra: وَٱلَّيْلِ وَمَا وَسَقَ continues the oath begun at 84:16 with night and what it gathers.
terra: وَٱلْقَمَرِ إِذَا ٱتَّسَقَ supplies the final object in the oath sequence begun by the section's formula at 84:16.

luna: The verse explicitly asks whether there is an oath, قَسَمٌ, in the preceding signs for a person of understanding. It makes the source section’s named root ق س م a question about how signs warrant an oath, rather than merely repeating the formula. | terra: هَلْ فِى ذَٰلِكَ قَسَمٌ لِّذِى حِجْرٍ calls the preceding divine oath sequence a qasam and asks the discerning listener to weigh it, complementing 56:76's description of an immense oath.

luna: This ayah says they do not honor the orphan. It adds the neglected recipient to the nearby rebuke in 89:18 about failing to urge food for the poor, directly reversing the source section’s orphan-and-feeding passage. | terra: بَل لَّا تُكْرِمُونَ ٱلْيَتِيمَ rebukes failure to honor the orphan, setting up the paired failure to promote feeding in 89:18.

luna: The verse reproaches people for not urging one another to feed the poor, عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ الْمِسْكِينِ. It is the direct opposite of the food passage that the source section presents as a way through. | terra: وَلَا تَحَاضُّونَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ ٱلْمِسْكِينِ is the direct negative counterpart to feeding the poor as passage and reparation.

luna: After 89:17–18’s neglect of the orphan and poor, this verse says they devour inheritance voraciously, وَتَأْكُلُونَ التُّرَاثَ أَكْلًا لَّمًّا. It reverses the source section’s image of a share distributed among a slain person’s kin and the garden owners’ attempt to reserve the harvest.

luna: This continues the same rebuke by naming their intense love of wealth, وَتُحِبُّونَ الْمَالَ حُبًّا جَمًّا. Its own contribution is the attachment that makes the exclusionary garden oath and withheld provision legible.
luna: This is another divine oath sequence whose final object is “this secure city,” وَهَٰذَا الْبَلَدِ الْأَمِينِ. The connection to 90:1 is the same sacred city, not merely the oath formula.

luna: This calls the Quraysh to worship رَبَّ هَٰذَا الْبَيْتِ, identifying the sanctuary in the immediate context of 106:4’s feeding against hunger. It supplies the local setting that joins the city oath to food provision.

luna: The verse says Allah fed the Quraysh against hunger and secured them from fear, أَطْعَمَهُم مِّن جُوعٍ. It connects the city named in the oath with the section’s feeding on a day of hunger; 106:3 identifies the sanctuary.

luna: This asks about the one who denies the Judgment, يُكَذِّبُ بِالدِّينِ, framing the orphan-repelling and refusal to urge food in 107:2–3. Its own contribution is to identify the stance behind those contrary acts, matching the section’s contrast with those who reject Allah’s signs. | terra: The denier of requital is introduced here, and the next two ayat identify that denial through repelling the orphan and refusing to urge food for the poor, paralleling the section's faith/deed boundary in reverse.

luna: The denier of the judgment pushes away the orphan, يَدُعُّ الْيَتِيمَ. This reverses the section’s care for the orphan and its account of the oath leading toward mercy. | terra: The denier يَدُعُّ ٱلْيَتِيمَ, reversing the surah's passage through care for the orphan.

luna: The same denier does not urge feeding the poor, عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ الْمِسْكِينِ. It is a precise contrary scene to the section’s food for the hungry. | terra: وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ ٱلْمِسْكِينِ makes failure even to urge feeding the poor a sign of denial, the negative counterpart of the section's feeding act.

luna: This concludes the same short portrait by saying they withhold small assistance, وَيَمْنَعُونَ الْمَاعُونَ. It adds a concrete form of deprivation beyond the failure to urge food in 107:3, opposite the section’s provisions for the needy.
